article_notes: Experimental B. rossi infection of five 6-month-old male beagles (3 high dose, 2 low dose) with serial sampling over 8 days, before and after diminazene treatment. The main comparisons are high vs low infectious dose and each time point vs baseline; dose group is an exposure, not a severity or outcome grouping, so those comparisons were not extracted. Extracted: (S1) the Spearman correlations the authors report between markers and parasitaemia, which they name as an indicator of disease severity; correlations are pooled over dogs and time points (number of observations not stated); the text gives the parasitaemia-IL-10 correlation twice with different r values (0.676 and 0.674, both p = 0.009). (S2) Descriptive statements about the single dog that died (high dose group, 96 h) vs the four survivors (n=1, no test). Parasitaemia measured on central venous blood. Correlations between pairs of inflammatory markers and CRP vs temperature are marker-marker and were not extracted.

severity_definitions.label: parasitaemia (continuous)
severity_definitions.definition: Venous parasitaemia (%) over the course of experimental infection, used by the authors as an indicator of disease severity; markers correlated with it by Spearman rank correlation across serial samples. Severity component is parasite burden (other).
severity_definitions.quote: we aimed to investigate changes in markers of inflammation (cytokine concentrations, neutrophil count, monocyte count and CRP) and indicators of disease severity (including habitus, appetite, vital parameters, parasitaemia and hematocrit) over time

severity_definitions.label: dog that died vs surviving dogs
severity_definitions.definition: One high dose dog died unexpectedly at about 96 hours, around the time of treatment; the other four inoculated dogs recovered.
severity_definitions.quote: Due to the unexpected death of one dog in the HD group, to avoid any further losses, the LD group was treated 12 hours later (at 108 hours)
